summary.name: IRC
summary.one_liner: Internet Relay Chat is a text-based, client-server group and private messaging protocol created in 1988, documented in RFC 1459.
use_cases: running a private chat server on a LAN
studying chat protocol history and design
connecting to open-source community chat networks
sharing files and sending private messages
summary.what_it_does: IRC is a text-based instant messaging protocol using a client-server model, where users connect a client to an IRC server that can be part of a larger network. It supports group discussion in channels (prefixed with # or &) as well as one-on-one private messages, and can carry data transfer such as file sharing. The page describes channel and user modes, operators, hostmasks, and the irc/ircs/irc6 URI schemes. It also covers the protocol's history, including the splits that created EFnet, Undernet, DALnet and IRCnet, and notes that it runs on TCP with optional TLS, typically on port 6667.
notable: Created by Jarkko Oikarinen in August 1988 at the University of Oulu; defined in RFC 1459
Has no official specification; many networks and clients diverge from RFC 1459
Newer IRCv3 standardization effort adds features like better history and notifications
Channel and user modes, IRC operators and services bots are central to the design
caveats: Usage has declined steadily since 2003, losing about 60 percent of users by 2012
Protocol lacks an official specification and character encoding is unspecified, causing client and server incompatibilities
No major IRC networks had fully adopted IRCv3 as of 2019 per the page
